Because this is urgent, please do one of these immediately:
1) Call the bank’s 24/7 card support line (the number printed on the back of your card and on your statement/website/app). Use the “lost or stolen card” option so they can block it and order a replacement right away.
2) If your bank’s mobile app or website has a “Lock card,” “Freeze card,” or “Report lost/stolen” option for the “Rewards Card ••••4321,” use that now. That typically blocks new charges instantly and lets you request a replacement.
3) If neither of the above is available, go to a branch as soon as you can and tell them your card is lost so they can block it and issue a new one.

- Watch for any unfamiliar charges.
- If you see a suspicious transaction, tell the phone rep or branch staff so they can open a dispute.

Once you’ve spoken with support or used the app to block it, tell me what they confirmed (blocked? replacement on the way? any temporary card?) and I can help you with next steps, like monitoring transactions or wording disputes if needed.</action>

1. Give a concise checklist of follow-up steps after a card is blocked and replacement ordered.
</plan>
<action type="say">
Here’s what I’d do next:

1) Review recent transactions  
- Look over the last 1–2 months of activity on that card.  
- Make a note of anything you don’t recognize, with dates and amounts, in case you need to dispute later.

2) Ask the bank about suspicious activity window (if they didn’t already say)  
- Confirm how far back they want you to check for fraudulent transactions.  
- Ask how to report any that you spot later (phone number / online form).

3) Update any recurring payments once the new card arrives  
Common places to update:  
- Streaming services, phone/internet, utilities  
- Subscriptions (software, music, cloud storage, gyms)  
- Ride-share, food delivery, online retailers  
- Any autopay billers using that card  
Your old card number won’t work anymore, so some payments could fail if you don’t update them.

4) Watch your accounts and alerts  
- Turn on transaction alerts (text/app/email) for the replacement card once you get it.  
- Keep an eye on your checking account too if it’s linked for payments to that card.

5) Check mail/email for any follow-up from the bank  
- They may send a fraud/affidavit form or a summary of what’s been blocked or credited.  
- Open and respond to anything time-sensitive.

If you’d like, tell me roughly which services you know are on that card (e.g., “phone bill, Netflix, gym”), and I can help you build a specific update checklist so you don’t miss any.</action>
